exceptions: full-ai-cluster/nixos/modules/k3s-datastore-preflight.sh — systemd ExecStartPre for k3s.service, not a shell-spawned child. The refusal it implements (a surviving server datastore on a box being re-flashed as a worker) must run BEFORE k3s starts, in a unit ordered ahead of it, so no stage-0 shell script can be its parent: `k3s-datastore-preflight.nix` sets ExecStart = bash ${preflightScript}. Routing it behind an existing door would mean running it after the thing it exists to gate. Kept a standalone .sh rather than inlined into the Nix string so its logic is EXECUTABLE against fixture disks in a unit test (see the module docstring) — a door admitted so the falsifier can reach it.

full-ai-cluster/nixos/modules/k3s-join-intent-preflight.sh — the sibling of k3s-datastore-preflight.sh above, admitted for the same structural reason and covering the case that one explicitly does not. It is a systemd oneshot ordered `before` k3s.service and `requiredBy` it, so no stage-0 shell script can be its parent: routing it behind an existing door would mean running it after the thing it exists to gate. It compares the join intent on disk (/etc/zeta/cluster-join-server-url) against what Nix evaluation actually RESOLVED, which is the only way to observe the pure-eval reversion `injected-server-join.nix` names in its own header — a joining server silently reverting to a FOUNDING one. The datastore preflight cannot catch it, by its own admission: "On a genuinely from-scratch flash that is fine — there is no datastore, so nothing is ignored", and a from-scratch flash is exactly how a second machine is added. Kept a standalone .sh rather than inlined into the Nix string so its logic is EXECUTABLE against fixtures in src/Core.TypeScript/hygiene/lint-k3s-join-intent-preflight.test.ts — a door admitted so the falsifier can reach it.
